title: Electronic Structure of Atoms - Chemistry - Aufbau
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The statement "Electrons fill the lowest energy orbitals available before filling higher energy orbitals" defines which principle?
questions.explain: The Aufbau Principle (German for 'building up') states that electrons occupy the lowest energy orbitals first.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which principle states that no two electrons in the same atom can have the exact same set of four quantum numbers?
questions.explain: The Pauli Exclusion Principle states that no two electrons can have the same four quantum numbers; therefore, an orbital can hold a maximum of two electrons with opposite spins.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Consider three electrons filling a $2p$ subshell. According to Hund's Rule, which configuration minimizes electron-electron repulsion and is most stable?
options: Two electrons in the first orbital, one in the second, zero in the third.
Three electrons in the first orbital.
One electron in each of the three orbitals, all with parallel spins.
One electron in each of the three orbitals, with alternating spins.
questions.explain: Hund's Rule states that for degenerate orbitals (like $p​$, $d​$, or $f​$), electrons fill each orbital singly with parallel spins before pairing up.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following orbital diagrams represents a violation of the Pauli Exclusion Principle?
options: An orbital containing two electrons with 'up' spin $(\uparrow\uparrow)$.
An orbital containing one electron with 'up' spin $(\uparrow)$.
An orbital containing two electrons with opposite spins $(\uparrow\downarrow)$.
Three degenerate orbitals each containing one electron $(\uparrow)(\uparrow)(\uparrow)$.
questions.explain: The Pauli Exclusion Principle requires that if two electrons occupy the same orbital, they must have opposite spins. Two electrons with the same spin $(\uparrow\uparrow)$ in one orbital is forbidden.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: According to the $(n+l)$ rule used in the Aufbau principle, which orbital is filled immediately after the $3p$ orbital?
questions.explain: Energy is determined by $n+l$. For $3p$: $3+1=4$. For $3d$: $3+2=5$. For $4s$: $4+0=4$. When $n+l$ is equal ($3p$ and $4s$), the one with lower $n​$ fills first ($3p$). The next lowest energy is $4s$ ($n+l=4$), which fills before $3d$ ($n+l=5$). So the order is $3p \rightarrow 4s$.
